draft.summary: The store's purchase rates vary significantly by month, with November showing the highest rate at 25.4%. New visitors have a notably higher purchase rate (24.9%) compared to returning visitors (13.9%). Visitors who spend more time and view more product pages are more likely to buy. Lower bounce and exit rates correlate with higher purchase likelihood. Traffic source 2 yields the highest purchase rate at 21.6%.

insights.title: November Shows Peak Purchase Rate
insights.finding: The purchase rate in November is 25.4% (2,998 sessions, 760 buyers), the highest among all months, while February has the lowest at 1.6% (184 sessions, 3 buyers).
insights.action: Focus marketing campaigns and inventory planning around November to capitalize on higher purchase rates, and investigate factors contributing to low February sales for improvement.

insights.title: New Visitors Purchase More Frequently Than Returning Ones
insights.finding: New visitors have a purchase rate of 24.9% (1,694 sessions, 422 buyers), which is higher than returning visitors at 13.9% (10,551 sessions, 1,470 buyers).
insights.action: Enhance first-time visitor experience and onboarding to maintain high purchase rates and convert new visitors into loyal customers.

insights.title: Higher Engagement on Product Pages Links to Purchases
insights.finding: Buyers view a median of 29.0 product pages and spend 18.5 minutes on product pages, compared to non-buyers who view 16.0 pages and spend 8.5 minutes. Correlations of ProductRelated (0.159) and ProductRelated_Duration (0.152) with purchase support this.
insights.action: Improve product page content and navigation to encourage longer browsing and more page views, potentially increasing purchase likelihood.

insights.title: Lower Bounce and Exit Rates Associate with Buying
insights.finding: Buyers have a median bounce rate of 0.0% and exit rate of 1.6%, while non-buyers have 0.4% bounce and 2.9% exit rates. Correlations of ExitRates (-0.207) and BounceRates (-0.151) with purchase are negative.
insights.action: Optimize landing pages and site flow to reduce bounce and exit rates, aiming to keep visitors engaged and increase purchases.

insights.title: Traffic Source 2 Drives Highest Purchase Rate
insights.finding: Traffic source 2 has a purchase rate of 21.6% (3,913 sessions, 847 buyers), outperforming other sources such as source 1 at 10.7% and source 3 at 8.8%.
insights.action: Allocate more marketing resources to traffic source 2 and analyze its characteristics to replicate its success across other channels.

insights.title: Weekend Visits Yield Higher Purchase Rates
insights.finding: Purchase rate on weekends is 17.4% (2,868 sessions, 499 buyers), higher than weekdays at 14.9% (9,462 sessions, 1,409 buyers).
insights.action: Consider targeted promotions or campaigns during weekends to leverage higher purchase propensity.

caveats: Purchase rates for months with fewer sessions (e.g., February with 184 sessions) may be less stable.
Traffic source 13 has a small sample size (738 sessions), so its purchase rate should be interpreted cautiously.
